exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
Place of birth (health institution vs. other)
outcome: Timely initiation of breastfeeding (within one hour of birth)
cohort: 472 mothers of infants less than six months old in Bahir Dar, Northwest, Ethiopia
finding: Vaginal delivery, giving birth at a health institution, and receiving breastfeeding counseling during antenatal care were significantly associated with timely initiation of breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Mothers who gave birth by vaginal delivery were more likely to initiate breastfeeding within one hour compared to those who underwent cesarean section.
